header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Samir Das (Redwood SE - joined briefly), Lena Ortiz (AuroraHealth CISO), Marcus Flynn (AuroraHealth Head of IT), Priya Shah (AuroraHealth Compliance)
summary: Redwood team reviewed SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture items for AuroraHealth. Discussed trust center access, controls mapping, audit log formats, SSO/RBAC integration, KMS/HSM options, data residency concerns, and evidence delivery for Aurora's internal audit. Agreed next steps: share SOC 2 report, provide Trust Center link and controls mapping, schedule technical deep dive on KMS/audit logs, and Aurora to provide residency/regulatory list.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya Patel from Redwood, AE on this account, with Jordan Lee our SE. Samir may pop in for a minute. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Lena: Hi Maya, thanks. Doing well. We want to walk through your SOC 2 and ISO posture, basically what evidence you can provide and how your trust center works.
[00:16] Marcus: Yeah, and sample audit logs we need to know retention and field mappings for our auditors.
[00:23] Jordan: Totally. We'll cover the reports we publish, what we can show in the trust center, and the controls mapping artifacts. Quick note: transcription might show "Redwood Dedicate" or "Redwood Privatee" that's just how auto transcribed.
[00:33] Priya: Haha noted.
[00:35] Maya: Cool. Quick agenda: 1) SOC 2 / ISO artifacts we can share, 2) Trust Center access and controls mapping, 3) SSO/RBAC and KMS questions, 4) audit logs and data residency, 5) next steps. Sound good?
[00:45] Lena: Yes. First - do you have a current SOC 2 Type II report and do you map it to ISO 27001 controls?
[00:52] Maya: We do. We have SOC 2 Type II for the last 12-month period I can share the attestation PDF. We also provide a controls mapping that crosswalks SOC 2 criteria to ISO 27001 clauses; it's in our trust center. Jordan, do you want to add details on what's in the mapping?
[01:05] Jordan: Yep. The mapping is a spreadsheet with SOC 2 control ID, description, evidence location, and ISO clause references. We also surface which controls are customer-configurable versus platform-managed.
[01:15] Marcus: Are there any parts of the control set that require auditor NDA or in-person review? Our auditors usually want service auditor access to evidence.
[01:23] Maya: We can provide redacted evidence and allow auditor access under an NDA. For some artifacts like internal change logs or vendor contracts, we can provide extracts. For deeper artifacts we coordinate with our security team and audit counsel.
[01:34] Priya: For evidence  is the trust center read-only? Can we give our auditors a link?
[01:38] Jordan: Yes, trust center has read-only links. We can provision a time-limited access token, and we also have a supplier portal for more formal audit access. I'll provision a read-only link for AuroraHealth.
[01:48] Samir (briefly): Also note we host the trust center in our compliance console link will have documented evidence, control owner notes, and the CSV export.
[01:55] Lena: Great. Next  encryption and KMS. We currently require CMEK with HSM-backed keys for certain PHI flows. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys that are HSM-backed?
[02:05] Jordan: Short answer: yes. We integrate with common KMS providers and can support BYOK with HSM-backed keys via vendor KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) or customer HSM in our Private deployment. For hosted, we support CMEK with customer KMS. There are caveats around key rotation and some metadata retention we have an integration guide.
[02:23] Marcus: What's retained in plaintext? Do you ever log plaintext or store decrypted content?
[02:28] Jordan: No plaintext persistence. The runtime handles decryption in-memory on the serving node and we persist only encrypted artifacts. Audit logs will show metadata like request ID, model variant, timestamps, but not plaintext content. Occasionally, debug bundles for support may contain masked snippets, and access to those is controlled and logged.
[02:44] Lena: Good. On audit logs we need field-level examples and retention options. Our policy: retain auth and admin logs for seven years, system logs for three years, and are flexible on request logs but usually two years. Can Redwood export logs to our SIEM or an S3 bucket?
[03:00] Jordan: We provide multiple log export options: streaming to customer SIEM via syslog/HTTPS, S3 push, or API pull. Retention is configurable for Dedicated and Private; hosted customers can request extended retention it's subject to add-on. I'll share sample log schema and a gzipped sample.
[03:14] Priya: Sample schema would be helpful. Also include fields for user_id, request_id, timestamp, model, token_count, action_type, response_status, and a flag for pii_redacted.
[03:26] Jordan: We'll include those fields. Note that for streaming we can include full structured JSON logs; we have a separate payload for audit-level events vs request-level telemetry.
[03:36] Maya: On SSO and RBAC do you support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC?
[03:42] Priya: This is key for us.
[03:44] Jordan: Yes SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM provisioning for user sync, and role-based access control with custom roles. For Private deployments you can set stricter org-wide controls. We also support 2FA enforced via IdP.
[03:56] Marcus: If we provision via SCIM, can we map groups to roles automatically?
[03:59] Jordan: Yes, group-to-role mapping is supported. We also have API endpoints for role assignments if you want programmatic control.
[04:07] Lena: Data residency our auditors require that data for EU patients stay in EU regions and never exit. How do you guarantee region locking?
[04:15] Jordan: For Dedicated and Private, you can pin deployment regions and we support region-locking. For hosted customers, we can route EU traffic to EU-only infrastructure and offer contractual data residency commitments; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll include our data residency whitepaper.
[04:29] Priya: Is there a SOC control that covers data residency specifically? We need mapping.
[04:33] Maya: In the controls mapping we annotate data-residency-related controls and where they live.
[04:38] Lena: Another ask  can we get the control descriptions mapped to our internal control IDs? We use a custom control matrix.
[04:44] Jordan: We can export the mapping CSV and you can map it to your IDs. If you share your control list, we can pre-map the ones that align.
[04:53] Marcus: Regarding logging for admin actions can we get change history for model deployments, rollback events, and who triggered them?
[04:59] Jordan: Yes, the audit log includes admin actions like model deploy, config changes, rollbacks, and the actor (SCIM user or service account). We keep those logs internally and can stream them to your SIEM.
[05:09] Lena: For ISO 27001 do you have an external certification or gap analysis?
[05:13] Maya: We maintain an ISO 27001 alignment and have completed an external gap assessment; we don't currently publish a certificate for all regions but we provide the mapping and evidence as part of the trust center. For enterprise customers we can share the assessment executive summary.
[05:26] Priya: Will auditors accept the mapping plus SOC 2 as evidence for ISO controls? Sometimes they want a dedicated ISO certificate.
[05:33] Jordan: It depends on the auditor. Many auditors accept the crosswalk plus SOC 2; others want a formal ISO 27001 cert. We can discuss options Dedicated/Private customers often request tailored evidence.
[05:44] Maya: Quick clarification on retention and e-discovery do you have a legal hold capability or can you export bulk logs on demand?
[05:51] Jordan: We can export bulk logs on demand; for legal hold we can snapshot relevant indices and store them to a customer S3 or archive. There may be operational lead time.
[06:01] Lena: What's the typical lead time to get trust center access and the SOC 2 PDF?
[06:05] Maya: I can share the SOC 2 PDF today via secure link and Jordan can provision trust center read-only in 24–48 hours.
[06:12] Jordan: I'll do the provisioning; Samir will upload the mapping CSV.
[06:16] Priya: One more for support escalations, do you provide SOC 2 style separation for support engineers? Our policy forbids support from accessing production data unless with explicit authorization.
[06:26] Jordan: We have support access controls and a break-glass workflow. Support access is audited and requires ticket-level approval for session access. We can show the audit trail for support sessions.
[06:36] Marcus: Do you have penetration testing reports or bug bounty info?
[06:39] Maya: We publish a pen-test summary and coordinate bounties; full reports are shared under NDA.
[06:44] Lena: Good. Let's talk about timeline our internal audit kickoff is July 10. We'll need evidence by July 3 to prepare. Can you commit to the deliverables by then?
[06:54] Maya: Yes SOC 2 file today, trust center and mapping by June 22, tech deep dive before June 25. That gives you time to assemble for July 3.
[07:03] Priya: Thank you. Can we also get the sample audit log file and the KMS integration guide?
[07:08] Jordan: Absolutely I'll attach sample logs (gzipped), KMS guide, and a short doc on key rotation semantics.
[07:16] Samir: Quick note sometimes the transcriber shows "KV cash" instead of KV cache, or K-M-S spelled out, so ignore those mismatches in the export.
[07:25] Maya: Okay pulling the recap: 1) I will share the SOC 2 Type II PDF (secure link) and the attestation. 2) Jordan will provision Trust Center read-only access and upload controls mapping CSV. 3) Jordan will also share sample audit log schema + sample gz log, and KMS integration guide. 4) AuroraHealth will send data residency/regulatory list and internal control IDs. 5) Schedule SE deep dive for KMS/audit logs — Marcus to own scheduling.
[07:49] Marcus: I'll schedule and loop in platform engineering.
[07:52] Lena: One last question for Dedicated, can we have SLA-backed log retention and longer retention within our contract?
[07:58] Jordan: Yes, retention SLAs and extended retention are contract options for Dedicated. We can scope in the PO.
[08:05] Priya: Perfect. That covers most of our questions. Thank you both.
[08:09] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links and timeline.
[08:13] Jordan: Thanks — talk soon.
[08:15] *meeting ends*

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts ("Dedicate" vs "Dedicated", "KV cash" vs "KV cache", "K-M-S" spelled out). Links to be provided after call: SOC2 PDF (secure link), Trust Center read-only link (time-limited), controls mapping CSV, sample_audit_log.json.gz, kms_integration_guide.pdf.

Recap / explicit next steps (same as action items above):
- Maya to share SOC 2 Type II report (link + PDF).
- Jordan to provision Trust Center access and upload controls mapping CSV.
- Jordan to provide sample audit log schema and KMS integration guide.
- AuroraHealth (Priya/Marcus) to provide residency requirements and internal control IDs.
- Schedule SE deep dive for KMS/audit logs prior to 2026-06-25.

End of transcript.
